title: Ancient Greece
intro: Gods, heroes, theatres and the very first Olympic Games.

questions.prompt: Where were the ancient Olympic Games held?
questions.explanation: The ancient Olympic Games were held at Olympia, in southern Greece, in honour of the god Zeus.

questions.prompt: Which Greek city-state was famous for its strong army and tough training?
questions.explanation: Sparta trained its boys to be soldiers from a young age and was known for its powerful army.

questions.prompt: Which ancient Greek city is known as the birthplace of democracy?
questions.explanation: In Athens, citizens could vote on decisions. This early form of democracy is still remembered today.

questions.prompt: In Greek myths, who was the king of the gods?
questions.explanation: Zeus ruled the gods from Mount Olympus and was the god of the sky and thunder.

questions.prompt: The ancient Greeks watched plays in open-air theatres.
questions.explanation: Greek theatres were built outdoors, often into hillsides, so large crowds could see and hear the actors.

questions.prompt: In the Greek myth, how did the Greeks get soldiers inside the city of Troy?

options.label: They hid inside a wooden horse

questions.explanation: The story says Greek soldiers hid inside a giant wooden horse, which the people of Troy pulled into their city.

questions.prompt: Which famous temple stands on the Acropolis in Athens?
questions.explanation: The Parthenon was built on the Acropolis hill as a temple to the goddess Athena.

questions.prompt: Athena was the Greek goddess of what?
questions.explanation: Athena was the goddess of wisdom and was also linked to war and crafts. Athens was named after her.

questions.prompt: The ancient Olympic Games were held every four years.
questions.explanation: The games took place every four years, a tradition the modern Olympics still follow.

questions.prompt: Poseidon was the Greek god of what?
questions.explanation: Poseidon, a brother of Zeus, was god of the sea and of earthquakes. He is often shown holding a three-pronged trident.

questions.prompt: According to Greek myths, where did the main family of gods live?
questions.explanation: The Greeks believed their gods lived in a palace in the clouds above Mount Olympus, the highest mountain in Greece.

questions.prompt: Hephaestus was the Greek god of what?
questions.explanation: Hephaestus was the blacksmith of the gods. He worked with fire to make weapons and armour for the other gods.

questions.prompt: In Greek myths, what kind of creature was Pegasus?
questions.explanation: Pegasus was a flying horse with wings, one of the best-loved creatures in Greek mythology.

questions.prompt: Which Greek hero found his way out of the Minotaur's maze by following a trail of string?
questions.explanation: Theseus unwound a ball of string as he went into the labyrinth, then followed it back to find his way out.

questions.prompt: In Greek myths, how many eyes did a Cyclops have?
questions.explanation: A Cyclops was a giant with a single eye in the middle of its forehead.

questions.prompt: Which Greek hero spent years at sea trying to sail home after the Trojan War?
questions.explanation: The poem the Odyssey tells how Odysseus faced monsters and storms on his long journey home to the island of Ithaca.

questions.prompt: Who was the wife of Zeus and queen of the gods?
questions.explanation: Hera was Zeus' wife and queen of the gods. She was the goddess of women, marriage and family.

questions.prompt: Which Greek god ruled the underworld?
questions.explanation: Hades, the elder brother of Zeus and Poseidon, ruled the underworld, where the Greeks believed people went after they died.

questions.prompt: Which ruler united the Greek city-states and built an empire stretching into Egypt and Asia?
questions.explanation: In the 300s BC, Alexander the Great brought the Greek city-states under one ruler and built a huge empire.

questions.prompt: What was the long, T-shirt-like piece of clothing that most ancient Greeks wore?
questions.explanation: Most Greeks wore a chiton, a long tunic made from one large piece of cloth.

questions.prompt: What did actors in ancient Greek plays wear on their faces?
questions.explanation: Greek actors wore masks that showed the audience whether a character was happy or sad. Some masks had two sides.

questions.prompt: What were winners at the earliest Olympic Games given?
questions.explanation: Victors at the first Olympics were crowned with a wreath of olive leaves. Medals came much later.

questions.prompt: The ancient Olympic Games were held in honour of which god?
questions.explanation: The Olympics were created to honour Zeus, king of the gods, and athletes prayed to him for victory.

questions.prompt: What name did the Romans give to the Greek hero Heracles?
questions.explanation: The Romans called Heracles 'Hercules'. He was famous for being incredibly strong and brave.

questions.prompt: Which bird was one of the sacred animals of the goddess Hera?
questions.explanation: Hera's sacred animals included the cow, the lion and the peacock, with its beautiful tail feathers.

questions.prompt: Just before the Olympic Games, the Greek city-states agreed a truce so people could travel safely.
questions.explanation: Even though city-states often quarrelled, they called a truce before the Games so athletes and visitors could reach Olympia safely.

questions.prompt: In ancient Greece, only men and boys were allowed to act in plays.
questions.explanation: Women and girls could not be actors, so men and boys played every part, including female characters.

questions.prompt: Hermes was the messenger of the gods.
questions.explanation: Hermes, a son of Zeus, carried messages for the gods. He is often shown with wings on his sandals.

questions.prompt: In what year BC are the first known Olympic Games said to have been held?
questions.explanation: The first known Olympic Games were held in 776 BC at Olympia, in southern Greece.

questions.prompt: In the Greek myth, how many difficult tasks did the hero Heracles have to complete?
questions.explanation: Heracles had to complete twelve tasks, known as his labours, such as defeating the many-headed Hydra.
